summary: This paper compares four freestanding multilayer Ti3C2Tx electrodes: pristine, Na+-pre-intercalated, K+-pre-intercalated, and Mg2+-pre-intercalated MXene. All were prepared by LiCl-assisted 10 wt % HF etching followed by HCl treatment and either HCl, NaCl, KCl, or MgCl2 soaking; electrodes contained 90 wt % MXene, 5 wt % carbon black, and 5 wt % PTFE. K−Ti3C2Tx was the headline/best electrode, reaching up to 300 F/g and ∼5.7 F/cm2 at 103 μm thickness and 20.1 mg/cm2 loading in 1 M H2SO4. The paper does not report BET area, pore size, porosity, tortuosity, flake lateral dimensions, or individual maximum areal capacitances for pristine and Mg−Ti3C2Tx.
